extracted.intended_audience: organizations and changemakers (local, regional, national) seeking grants, sponsorships, or awards from the Kauffman Foundation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the Kauffman Foundation's funding philosophy, the attributes they look for in projects, strategic priority areas, focus areas, and the types of funding opportunities they offer over the next 10 years to advance economic mobility.

rubrics_metrics.name: proximity to community
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the foundation's four-pillar framework values: proximity to community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding philosophy emphasizes closeness to community — projects should be rooted in and responsive to community needs and perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: getting uncomfortable
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the foundation's four-pillar framework values: getting uncomfortable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation is dedicated to doing hard things for innovation and possibility; applicants should be willing to take bold, potentially uncomfortable approaches to address problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: achieving impact
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the foundation's four-pillar framework values: achieving impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded work should aim to produce measurable, meaningful advances in economic mobility and related outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: creating hope
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the foundation's four-pillar framework values: creating hope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should contribute to a sense of possibility and improved prospects for learners and communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: research-informed, focused, coherent strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation pursues a focused, coherent, research-informed strategy to reach its goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should be grounded in evidence or research, aligned with a clear strategy, and demonstrate how they contribute to the foundation's long-term goals (closing economic mobility gaps in Kansas City).

rubrics_metrics.name: ignite potential and drive uncommon results
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation seeks projects that 'ignite potential and drive uncommon results.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should propose work with high upside — transformative or unusually strong results relative to typical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: bold innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation values bold innovation in projects it funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that introduce novel approaches or reimagine systems are prioritized; being innovative is a positive selection factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: collective impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation emphasizes collective impact as a desirable project attribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborative, cross-organizational efforts that coordinate toward shared goals are favored over isolated, siloed interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: transparency and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation looks for transparency and accountability in funded work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should propose clear metrics, reporting practices, and mechanisms for accountability to stakeholders and funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: support for local, regional, and national changemakers
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation supports local, regional, and national changemakers to unlock learner potential and remove barriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may be local, regional, or national organizations; proposals should explain their relevance and anticipated impact at the appropriate scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: unlock learner potential / remove barriers / rethink future of work and learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority outcomes include unlocking learner potential, clearing pathways and removing barriers, and rethinking the future of work and learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should target measurable improvements in learner outcomes, accessibility, transitions to work, and system redesigns that address barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: engage, listen, share successes and failures, and continuously adapt
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation seeks partners who engage with communities, listen, share successes and failures, and continuously adapt based on feedback and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should describe mechanisms for community engagement, learning practices, plans to evaluate and iterate, and willingness to be transparent about both successes and failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: willingness to do hard things / embrace discomfort for innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: A stated organizational commitment: 'We are more dedicated than ever to doing hard things – even if uncomfortable – for the sake of innovation and possibility.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that confront entrenched problems, take calculated risks, or challenge conventional approaches align with this expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: strategic priorities: college access and completion; workforce and career development; entrepreneurship
rubrics_metrics.description: Three prioritized strategies: college access and completion, workforce and career development, and entrepreneurship — chosen for their anticipated power to advance economic mobility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects aligned with one or more of these three strategies are prioritized; applicants should articulate how their work contributes to these specific strategic goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: focus_area: essential competencies and skills
rubrics_metrics.description: One of four focus areas: essential competencies and skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals addressing foundational skills and competencies essential for learning and workforce success are within scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: focus_area: education and employer connection
rubrics_metrics.description: One of four focus areas: education and employer connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that strengthen links between education systems and employers (e.g., pathways, partnerships, work-based learning) are prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: focus_area: participation and belonging
rubrics_metrics.description: One of four focus areas: participation and belonging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiatives that increase inclusive participation and a sense of belonging among learners and communities are desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: focus_area: equitable access
rubrics_metrics.description: One of four focus areas: equitable access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should address disparities and expand equitable access to opportunities and supports that advance economic mobility.

rubrics_metrics.name: funding mechanisms: grants (ongoing cycle)
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation offers grants through an ongoing cycle; funding amounts, grant terms, and application criteria vary by type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should review specific grant opportunities for eligibility, amounts, terms, and application instructions before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: funding_mechanism: sponsorships must align with mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsorships: specific funds are dedicated each year to sponsor events that connect people and raise funding for vital programs aligned with the foundation's mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Event sponsorship requests should demonstrate clear alignment with the foundation's mission and goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: funding_mechanism: awards recognize community champions
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards: the foundation recognizes and celebrates community champions and bold changemakers having impact in the Kansas City area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are for recognition of demonstrated community impact in the KC area rather than standard project funding; applicants/nominees should show local impact.
